question.text: Which of the following best describes Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs)?

answer.text: Mutual funds that can only be bought during NFO
Mutual funds that track an index and are traded on stock exchanges like stocks throughout the day
Closed-ended funds that are mandatorily listed

explanation.text: The Logic: ETFs are mutual funds that are usually index-tracking, listed and traded on stock exchanges throughout the day with real-time prices, and settled via demat accounts through brokers. Unlike regular open-ended funds which have a single daily NAV, ETFs have multiple intraday prices. The Trap: ETFs are not limited to NFO purchase — after listing, they are bought and sold on stock exchanges through brokers, with settlement in demat form. Note: After the NFO, ETF units are transacted on the exchange like shares, requiring a demat account and a broker.
